title: Robustness of Skyrmion-Mediated Magnetization Switching in Perpendicular Magnetic Tunnel Junctions (p-MTJs) to Material Disorder and Elevated Temperature
authors: Prosenjit Das, Md Mahadi Rajib, Jayasimha Atulasimha
abstract: Transient-skyrmion mediated voltage-controlled magnetic anisotropy (VCMA) switching is a fast and energy efficient way to magnetization reversal, but its reliability under realistic material disorder and thermal fluctuations remain unclear. In this work, we use stochastic micromagnetic simulations of a 100 nm perpendicular magnetic tunnel junction to study switching reliability under grain-scale variations in Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction, perpendicular magnetic anisotropy, easy-axis orientation, and intergrain exchange coupling. We find that switching remains robust under moderate disorder, with 100% switching observed in 10^4 stochastic simulations after pulse width optimization at both 300 K and 350 K. Increasing the temperature from 300 to 350 K shifts the optimum VCMA pulse width from ~475 to ~450 ps, indicating that an apparent reduction in switching probability at a fixed pulse duration can be primarily due to pulse detuning. In contrast, strong easy-axis disorder reduces the maximum switching probability even after pulse-width optimization, indicating degradation of the switching dynamics. We further show that, under strong easy-axis disorder a transient skyrmion still forms while the subsequent post-pulse dynamics fails to complete the magnetization reversal. Our study therefore establishes the distinction between recoverable reliability due to timing shifts and permanent disorder-induced degradation that simply cannot be recovered by pulse re-tuning. Finally, for no disorders but at room temperature, 100% switching is observed with 10^6 stochastic simulations with correct pulse shaping.
summary: This work simulates magnetization switching in p-MTJs using stochastic micromagnetics to test reliability under disorder and heat. It finds that while timing errors can be corrected by adjusting the electrical pulse, strong material disorder causes permanent degradation of the switching mechanism. This establishes a critical distinction between recoverable timing issues and fundamental material limitations.
main_problem: The paper assesses the reliability of skyrmion-mediated magnetization switching in p-MTJs when subjected to realistic material disorder and elevated temperature.
main_result: The study distinguishes between recoverable reliability loss due to timing shifts (which can be fixed by pulse re-tuning) and permanent degradation caused by strong disorder.
method: Stochastic micromagnetic simulations were employed to model magnetization dynamics governed by the LLG equation.
model_or_system: The system is a 100 nm perpendicular magnetic tunnel junction (p-MTJ) modeled with a polycrystalline structure exhibiting grain-scale variations in Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI), perpendicular magnetic anisotropy (PMA), and easy-axis orientation.
key_observables: Switching probability (P_sw), out-of-plane magnetization (m_z), and topological charge (Q).
important_parameters: Temperature (300 K to 350 K), disorder strength (e.g., 15% DMI/PMA variation, 6% easy-axis misalignment), and pulse width (optimized vs. fixed).
main_assumptions: The dynamics are governed by the LLG equation, and disorder is modeled using Gaussian random variables over a Voronoi tessellation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the dependence of P_sw on pulse width and temperature, comparing defect-free, moderately disordered, and strongly disordered structures, and comparing switching trajectories under different disorder levels.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes baseline switching reliability, then analyzes the effect of temperature shifts on optimal pulse timing, and finally contrasts the effects of moderate versus strong disorder, concluding with a clear distinction between timing-related and structure-related failure modes.
why_interesting: While focused on magnetism, the methodology of analyzing failure modes due to quenched disorder (e.g., easy-axis misalignment) and thermal fluctuations maps conceptually onto studying robustness in complex quantum systems or spin glasses.
